source_text: Quamvis in hoc quoque clementia Dei uberior approbetur, quoniam sanctificat parvulos nescientes; ad laudem quippe misericordiae respicit, cum eos nescientes culpa non inquinet; ad leges enim id pertinet aequitatis.
pass_a_gloss: Although in this also the clemency of God is approved more abundant, since he sanctifies little ones not knowing; for it looks to the praise of mercy, when guilt does not stain them not knowing; for that pertains to the laws of fairness.

lemmas.lexica: LS parvulus; Blaise infants without usus rationis

pass_b_english: God’s mercy is nevertheless shown still richer in this: he sanctifies infants who do not know it. That belongs to the praise of mercy, whereas their ignorance leaves them unstained by guilt; that belongs to the laws of fairness.

choices.why: Speechless newborns without rational choice; Julian's test case against inherited sin.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
